T: Bread, circuses and a proper Roman feast.
D: Years after Maximus, Lucius is captured in North Africa and forced to fight in the Colosseum.
P: Serve the mains when the emperors throw their banquet.
S: Medjool dates stuffed with toasted almonds and pepper, fried in butter, then glazed in hot honey and sea salt, the old Roman way. Toast 24 whole almonds in a dry pan for 4 minutes. Slit and pit 24 Medjool dates, push an almond and a grind of black pepper into each and press closed. Melt 30g butter in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the dates 2 minutes, turning, until warm and glossy. Add 3 tbsp honey and let it bubble for 1 minute, turning the dates to coat. Tip onto a plate and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Macrinus's baked feta with figs and honey
Macrinus, the dealer who buys Lucius

A block of feta baked in olive oil with oregano and chilli, topped with roasted figs, thyme and honey, with warm olives and crusty bread. Heat the oven to 200C. Put a 200g block of feta in a small baking dish with 150g mixed olives around it. Halve 4 fresh figs and nestle them in. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil and sprinkle with dried oregano, chilli flakes and thyme sprigs. Bake 15 minutes until the feta is soft. Drizzle with 2 tbsp honey and serve with torn crusty bread.

Thin flatbreads blistered in a hot pan, brushed with garlic and rosemary oil, sprinkled with sea salt and served with labneh for dipping. Mix 300g self-raising flour, 250g Greek yoghurt and half a tsp salt into a dough and rest 10 minutes. Warm 4 tbsp olive oil with 2 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tbsp chopped rosemary for 3 minutes. Divide the dough into 8, roll thin and cook in a hot dry pan 1 to 2 minutes a side until charred in spots. Brush with the rosemary oil and sprinkle with flaky salt. Serve with 250g labneh drizzled with oil.
M: Whole chicken roasted with honey, garlic, thyme and lemon until sticky and golden, with roast vegetables.
Numidian lamb, apricot and chickpea stew

Lamb shoulder braised with chickpeas, tomato, cumin, cinnamon and dried apricots, spooned over fluffy couscous with harissa yoghurt and mint. Brown 1kg diced lamb shoulder in batches in oil. Fry 2 onions for 5 minutes, add 3 garlic cloves, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp cinnamon and 1 tsp paprika. Add 400g tinned tomatoes, 500ml stock and the lamb, cover and simmer 1.5 hours. Add 400g drained chickpeas and 120g dried apricots and cook 30 minutes. Pour 300ml boiling stock over 300g couscous, cover 5 minutes. Swirl 1 tbsp harissa through 200g yoghurt. Serve with mint.
W: Ricotta mixed with honey, egg and lemon zest, baked until set and drizzled with more honey.
K: the twin emperors Geta and Caracalla at their banquet

Red wine warmed gently with honey, black pepper, cinnamon, bay and orange peel, the spiced wine of ancient Rome, served warm in heavy cups. Pour a 750ml bottle of red wine into a saucepan with 4 tbsp honey, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 black peppercorns, 2 bay leaves and 3 strips of orange peel. Warm gently over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring until the honey dissolves. Do not let it boil. Strain into 4 heavy cups. For non-drinkers, make it the same way with red grape juice and less honey.

m.how: Rub a 1.8kg whole chicken with oil, salt, crushed garlic and thyme and stuff with a halved lemon. Roast at 200C on a bed of 6 carrots for 60 minutes, then brush with 3 tbsp honey and roast 15 minutes more until sticky. Rest 10 minutes and carve.

w.how: Beat 500g ricotta with 3 eggs, 4 tbsp honey and the zest of 1 lemon until smooth. Pour into a lined 20cm tin and bake at 170C for 40 minutes until just set. Cool and drizzle with 2 tbsp more honey.
